children.text: Portugal is one of the most popular destinations for digital nomads, and it's no surprise, here you'll find a sunny climate, historic architecture, fast internet, and a comfortable lifestyle.
The digital nomad visa allows you to settle in any city in Portugal, meaning you can choose bustling Lisbon, quiet seaside Porto, or even the peaceful, tropical Madeira.

In today's blog, we'll go through those cities in Portugal that are most appealing to digital nomads - taking into account various factors such as living conditions, costs, workspaces, and quality of life.
Lisbon

Lisbon stands out for its large community of freelancers, where meetups, stand-up comedy shows, knowledge-sharing evenings, co-working days, and much more are held very frequently, allowing you to develop and diversify your social circle and contacts. Lisbon is also known for its sunny, pleasant weather. And most importantly, Lisbon always has fast internet, allowing you to work without interruptions.
If you miss working in an office while in Lisbon, that's not a problem either, since Lisbon has plenty of coworking spaces, with daily rates starting from €15.

As for living costs: renting an apartment in Lisbon is somewhat more expensive compared to other cities, but on the outskirts of the city you can rent an apartment at quite an affordable price. For example, you can rent a two-room apartment for around €1,500, and a one-room apartment for €500–600. Getting around is very convenient - for example, a monthly metro pass costs €40.
Algarve
If seaside living appeals to you, then Algarve is the ideal place for you. Algarve has the largest community of digital nomads, providing a friendly and inspiring atmosphere for nomads.

Algarve has created many spaces and events where you can expand both your professional and social networks. Coworking meetups, sports and entertainment activities, and cultural events are frequently held here.

Living costs are relatively lower compared to Lisbon, though prices in popular tourist spots vary seasonally. A 1-room apartment rents for €400–600 on average; a 2-room apartment for €900–1,200. Getting between cities is easy, and public transport within the region is well developed.
Madeira
Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic Ocean, one of the most popular and in-demand locations for digital nomads.

Madeira is one of the first places in Europe where living and working spaces were specifically created for digital nomads. Ponta do Sol is the first nomad village, where you can work, live, and take part in various events. The island has many public workspaces set up, where you can work in a peaceful environment and connect with other nomads.

Madeira's climate is ideal — even winter here is warm and comfortable. In Madeira, you can start your day with a laptop in a café and end the evening surfing or hiking against a lavender-colored sky. Cafés and workspaces are well equipped, and coworking spaces cost around €10–20 per day. Renting an apartment in Madeira is relatively cheap, though prices are rising along with growing demand. A 1-room apartment rents for €600–800; a 2-room apartment ranges from €1,000–1,500.
Porto
If you want a calm but dynamic environment, stunning architecture, riverside views, and a high quality of life at a lower price, Porto is the ideal choice.

In recent years, Porto has been actively attracting digital nomads, which is why the city has a variety of coworking spaces and comfortable cafés where you can work with stable Wi-Fi in a peaceful setting.
Porto is known for its active cultural life - knowledge-sharing evenings, creative industry meetups, and freelancer events are frequently held here.

Porto's climate is relatively cooler and damper compared to Lisbon and Algarve, but summers here are still lovely and warm, while winter is mild and humid. Porto is also more affordable than Lisbon, meaning you can enjoy a higher quality of life at a lower cost.
On average: a 1-room apartment rents for €500–700; a 2-room apartment for €900–1,200. Getting around the city is simple by metro or bus, with a monthly pass costing around €40.
Ericeira

If surfing, seaside living, and a calm yet active nomad environment matter to you, then you should try living in Ericeira! This small but lively town is one of the most attractive locations in Portugal for digital nomads.

In recent years, Ericeira has become one of the most popular hubs for digital nomads, with many coworking spaces and frequent nomad events. After a tiring workday, you can relax at seaside bars or go surfing.

The town is known for its clean air, golden beaches, and stunning ocean views, creating an ideal environment not only for relaxation but also for boosting productivity. Living in Ericeira is budget-friendly. A 1-room apartment rents for €500–800; a 2-room apartment for €900–1,300.
You can get around town by public transport, bike, or on foot, and the connection to Lisbon is easy by bus, which runs regularly (the trip takes about 45 minutes).
